Senses.Explanation: Master Zhigong is the pre-Zen figure whom Chan records quote, identify with a direct answer, and place in exchanges at Emperor Wu's court. His name occurs 494 times in 133 allowlisted texts. Asked "what is buddha?" a master answers, "Master Zhigong" (誌公和尚); when challenged, he says, "Zhigong is not an idle monk" (誌公不是閑和尚). In the Fu Dashi case, Fu mounts the seat, strikes the desk once, and descends; Zhigong asks Emperor Wu whether he understands, then says, "the great man has finished lecturing the scripture" (大士講經竟). Later masters repeatedly quote and criticize that verdict. His sayings are also treated as named textual material: the Twelve-Hour Song, Fourteen Sections, and Great-Vehicle Praises. Zen therefore deploys Zhigong as a named answer to "what is buddha?," court interlocutor and adjudicator of Fu Dashi's action, and quoted author.
Senses.Note: One person sense. Zhigong (誌公), Master Zhigong (誌公和尚), and Baozhi (寶誌公) name the same figure in this corpus. Titles of works attributed to him are named works, not a second sense of the bare personal name.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。如何是佛。師曰。誌公和尚。曰。學人問佛。何故答誌公和尚。師曰。誌公不是閑和尚。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元): Wanan Daoyan answers an unnamed monk's question 'what is Buddha?' with 'Preceptor Baozhi' and then insists that Baozhi is not an idle monk.

Occurrences.Kwic: 梁武帝請講金剛經，士纔陞座，以尺揮按一下，便下座，帝愕然。誌公曰：陛下會麼？帝曰：不會。誌公曰：大士講經竟。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Shanhui Dashi (善慧大士語錄): after Fu Dashi leaves the lecture seat, Baozhi asks Emperor Wu whether he understands and declares the great man's scripture lecture finished.

Occurrences.Kwic: 却被誌公云陛下還會麼。帝云。不會。誌公云。大士講經竟也。是一人作頭。一人作尾。誌公恁麼道。還夢見傅大士麼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Blue Cliff Record of Chan Master Foguo Yuanwu (佛果圜悟禪師碧巖錄). Baozhi is the exact speaker who asks Emperor Wu whether he understands and then says Fu Dashi has finished lecturing; Yuanwu Keqin subsequently criticizes Baozhi's verdict.

Occurrences.Kwic: 誌公和尚大乘讚十首誌公和尚十二時頌十二首誌公和尚十四科頌
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄): the compiler's table of verse and praise collections lists Baozhi's ten Mahayana Praises, twelve Twelve-Hours Songs, and Fourteen-Section Verses; Baozhi is the named author, while the headword occurs in documentary catalog prose rather than a speech turn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 誌公和尚云。內外追尋覔總無。境上施為渾大有。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Changqing Da'an section. Baozhi (Zhigong) is explicitly introduced as the quoted speaker of the contrast between finding nothing through inner and outer search and abundant activity on objects.

Occurrences.Kwic: 被誌公和尚一喝曰。大士莫作是說。別更道看。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元): inside the case raised in Foxing Fatai's section, Baozhi is the exact speaker who shouts at Fu Dashi, tells him not to speak that way, and asks him to say something else.
